newFindings.title: HDL-only Execute throws an icon ClassCastException and strands the commander
newFindings.verification: Fresh live reproduction plus current source and recovered log.
newFindings.observed: Generate HDL only > Execute immediately disables the clock, annotation, board and action controls. Progress remains Idle; no visible error is shown. The log records FlatSVGIcon cannot be cast to ProjectAddIcon at FpgaCommander.java:404, before Download is constructed.
reproduction: Open a disposable project.
FPGA > Synthesize & Download; leave Generate HDL only selected.
Click Execute; inspect disabled controls and app log.
newFindings.rootCause: StopButton receives an SVG icon, but start, stop and completion still cast it to the removed ProjectAddIcon type. Execute disables controls before the failing cast.
newFindings.fix: Remove all three obsolete casts; express stop state with button enabled/state and the SVG icon API. Restore controls and show an actionable error on every failed start or worker exit.
newFindings.acceptance: With no vendor software installed, Generate HDL only starts the internal generation/DRC path and either produces files in a temporary destination or presents a useful design error. Repeat start, cancel, and retry without a ClassCastException or stranded controls. Run external download checks separately when a board/toolchain exists.
newFindings.limits: External synthesis/programming was not attempted; this failure occurs before any toolchain is invoked.

newFindings.title: Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab do not cycle circuit tabs from the canvas
newFindings.verification: Fresh live forward/reverse checks; Ctrl+W positive control.
newFindings.observed: With main and inv open, canvas focus followed by Ctrl+Tab left main selected. With three tabs open, Ctrl+Shift+Tab from inv left inv selected. Ctrl+W from the same canvas successfully closed inv.
reproduction: Open at least two circuits from the Circuits list.
Click empty canvas to give it focus.
Press Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab; compare active editor tabs.
Press Ctrl+W as a positive control.
newFindings.rootCause: The shortcuts are installed in the tab strip's WHEN_IN_FOCUSED_WINDOW map. No corresponding focus-traversal override was found on Canvas/EditorTabs. Traversal interception is the likely cause, not yet instrumented; live failure is established.
newFindings.fix: Trace the focus manager's consumed key events and route next/previous-editor actions at the owning root pane/focus boundary, excluding those chords from traversal where necessary. Keep ordinary Tab and text-editor behavior intact.
newFindings.acceptance: At least three circuit/HDL tabs wrap forward and backward from canvas, circuit list, filter, and code editor focus. Ctrl+W still closes one tab; normal Tab traverses controls with visible focus.
newFindings.limits: Window-manager and platform portability beyond the private Linux KWin/Xwayland session is untested.

newFindings.title: Oscillation stops propagation without synchronizing the run controls
newFindings.verification: Recovered images actually viewed; current source confirms missing state notification. Not freshly reproduced.
newFindings.observed: Recovered osc2 captures show Oscillation apparent and a paused status, while the toolbar still offers Pause and the Simulate menu still checks Auto-Propagate.
reproduction: Use the recovered simtest2.circ oscillator fixture in a fresh disposable copy.
Open osc2 and poke en to trigger sustained oscillation.
Compare the canvas/status error with the toolbar and Auto-Propagate menu state.
newFindings.rootCause: The oscillation branch clears autoPropagating and autoPropagatingUnsynchronized, but the later fireSimulatorStateChanged call is gated only by clockDied. A propagation-completed notification does not update all run-state controls.
newFindings.fix: Emit a simulator state-change event when oscillation changes automatic propagation, with UI updates dispatched consistently to the EDT. Keep the error visible and make reset/recovery state explicit.
newFindings.acceptance: After a deliberately triggered oscillation, Auto-Propagate is unchecked and the toolbar shows Resume/Run everywhere it appears. Reset clears the error and a subsequent start updates all controls.
newFindings.limits: This is misleading state feedback, not evidence of data loss or incorrect saved circuit data.

newFindings.title: SoC transaction dialog identifies the target bus as null
newFindings.verification: Recovered native window capture viewed; exact current source cause identified.
newFindings.observed: The dialog title reads Insert a transaction to bus: null, although the memory-map window can identify the bus.
reproduction: In a disposable SoC fixture, right-click a bus.
Choose Insert a bus transaction.
Inspect the dialog title.
newFindings.rootCause: actionPerformed passes info.getName(), the inherited JMenuItem component name. The constructors call super(label) but never set that name. The resulting null is concatenated into the window title.
newFindings.fix: Carry an explicit bus display name or derive it from the instance label with the existing type@coordinates fallback. Do not use the Swing component name as domain identity.
newFindings.acceptance: Transaction windows for two differently named/unnamed buses show distinct correct names, including a stable fallback for an unlabeled bus. No title contains null.
newFindings.limits: Recovered SoC visuals only; bus execution was not rerun in this review.

newFindings.title: Recovered TCL/HDL editor open logs X11 Window must not be zero
newFindings.verification: Recovered stack inspected; not reproduced on this session or a normal desktop.
newFindings.observed: app-run3.log contains IllegalArgumentException: Window must not be zero while HdlContentEditor.setVisible calls Dialog.setVisible through an attribute editor.
reproduction: Place a TCL generic component in a disposable project.
Open its HDL interface/content attribute editor.
Check modal ownership and whether opening succeeds repeatedly.
newFindings.rootCause: Undetermined; stack implicates native X11 transient/modal ownership. A private compositor or disposed owner may contribute. Do not label it a universal production crash.
newFindings.fix: First reproduce with a visible normal desktop and a fresh owner window; then fix owner lifecycle/modal creation only if reproduced. Record JDK/window-manager versions.
newFindings.acceptance: Repeated open/close from a live project works without an X11 exception on supported desktops; a private-rig-only failure is tracked against the harness.
newFindings.limits: No severity assigned until the effect and reproduction boundary are established.

relatedFindings.title: Drawer and panel resizing snaps back; default timing/test-vector content is unusably short
relatedFindings.verification: Fresh live divider drags and vector run, backed by source.
relatedFindings.observed: Both tested divider positions remain unchanged after dragging. Timing shows only the ruler; loaded test vectors report 2 passed/2 failed but have no visible result rows at the default drawer height.
reproduction: Open Timing diagram and select clk.
Drag the drawer divider upward and the Circuits divider rightward.
Open inv > Test Vector and load the copied inv_test.txt.
relatedFindings.rootCause: Continuous split layout reapplies the remembered size before drag release can persist the new size. Drawer migration/minimum is in unscaled pixels, so the existing height is inadequate at 1.6.
relatedFindings.fix: Apply restored sizes during initialization/explicit relayout only, permit live dragging, and persist the released size. Derive the drawer's initial/minimum useful height from its controls and font metrics; keep body scrolling available.
relatedFindings.acceptance: At 1.0, 1.6 and 2.0 scales, drag every splitter smoothly, reopen with sizes retained, and inspect a visible waveform plus at least four test rows. A 2-pass/2-fail vector exposes each failed cell and Show/Set actions.
relatedFindings.reason: Same shared splitter defect as shell-03. Hidden timing/test rows are downstream effects, not two extra bugs.

relatedFindings.title: Circuit list loses its listener to garbage collection and becomes stale
relatedFindings.verification: Fresh live GC, tab-switch and F2 rename; source establishes lifetime defect.
relatedFindings.observed: After jcmd GC.run on the private JVM, main is active while inv remains selected in the list. Renaming osc to osc_qa updates the tab and title while the list still displays osc.
reproduction: Open main and inv from the list.
Allow GC or request GC only on a disposable QA JVM.
Click main tab and compare list highlight.
Select osc, press F2, rename to osc_qa; compare row and tab.
relatedFindings.rootCause: MyListener is a constructor-local variable registered with weak project/library event sources. CircuitListView does not retain it strongly.
relatedFindings.fix: Retain the listener in a field for the view lifetime, unregister on disposal, and keep current-circuit selection and library mutations synchronized. Guard actions against targets no longer in the project.
relatedFindings.acceptance: After forced GC, add/rename/delete/reorder/set-main and tab switching update the list immediately. Undo/redo does the same. A deleted row cannot be reopened as a ghost.
relatedFindings.reason: Unifies add/rename, stale highlight, and recovered deleted-row symptoms. No data-loss claim: ghost editing/saving was not retested.

relatedFindings.title: Chronogram ruler baseline clips timestamp and cursor text
relatedFindings.verification: Fresh ruler crop and recovered populated waveform crop actually viewed; current code checked.
relatedFindings.observed: The tops of timestamps and the highlighted cursor label disappear above the ruler. This remains visible in recovered images with a taller drawer.
reproduction: Open Timing diagram at 1.6.
Generate ticks and inspect the ruler at native pixels; enlarge drawer after fixing the splitter.
relatedFindings.rootCause: Fixed 20-pixel header and h/2 baseline are incompatible with the scaled monospaced font.
relatedFindings.fix: Compute header/row dimensions and baselines from font ascent/descent and scaled padding. Size signal-name/value columns for useful content.
relatedFindings.acceptance: Ruler and cursor labels are entirely inside their bounds at all supported scales, with no overlap at minimum and enlarged drawer sizes.
relatedFindings.reason: Visual corroboration of the existing codeaudit-08 cause; not another drawer-resize bug.

relatedFindings.title: Code editor theme resets code to a smaller font than its gutter and surrounding UI
relatedFindings.verification: Recovered VHDL pixels viewed and EditorTheme code checked; not freshly opened.
relatedFindings.observed: The VHDL screenshot shows much larger gutter numbers than code, with the surrounding shell using larger scaled text.
reproduction: Create/open VHDL content at 1.6 interface scale.
Compare code, line numbers, and shell labels; switch editor theme.
relatedFindings.rootCause: Theme.load(input).apply(editor) has no explicit scaled base font; the editor/gutter font contract is inconsistent.
relatedFindings.fix: Apply the shared scaled mono font to syntax styles and gutter together, retaining it across theme changes. Review assembler and breakpoint editors using the same helper.
relatedFindings.acceptance: Code and gutter use aligned line metrics at 1.0, 1.6 and 2.0, including after a theme change. Verify actual rendered text, not only font property values.
relatedFindings.reason: Same EditorTheme root cause as codeaudit-07; no per-editor inflation.

relatedFindings.title: SoC memory-map table uses unreadable blue headers and inconsistent row colors
relatedFindings.verification: Recovered native memory-map screenshot viewed; current renderer code checked.
relatedFindings.observed: Header text is saturated blue on dark gray; allocated/empty rows use bright accent and light gray backgrounds with black text. The component-name header and values are truncated.
reproduction: Open Show memory map on a SoC bus in dark theme.
Inspect header contrast and complete component names at 1.6.
relatedFindings.rootCause: Hard-coded primary colors and fixed table presentation bypass the shared dark/light table styling.
relatedFindings.fix: Use semantic themed table foreground/background and selection colors; reserve warning styling for overlaps and size/scroll columns to retain addresses and component identity.
relatedFindings.acceptance: Native captures of empty, mapped and overlapping regions remain readable in dark/light themes at 1.0 and 1.6; color is not the only overlap indicator.
relatedFindings.reason: Corroborates the existing shared FPGA/SoC renderer finding.

relatedFindings.title: Welcome actions are mouse-only panels
relatedFindings.verification: Source confirmed only in this review; original keyboard notes used as leads.
relatedFindings.observed: WelcomePanel.action creates JPanel/JLabel rows and only adds a mouseClicked handler; no focusable action/button or keyboard activation is installed.
reproduction: Fresh launch with isolated home and preferences.
Attempt Tab/Shift+Tab, Enter and Space on New/Open/recent-file rows.
relatedFindings.rootCause: Actions are represented as passive panels rather than keyboard-accessible controls.
relatedFindings.fix: Use shared Swing Actions with styled buttons or implement focusability, visible focus, Enter/Space activation and accessible names on each row.
relatedFindings.acceptance: A keyboard-only user can reach and activate New, Open and recent files with clear focus, with global shortcuts still working.
relatedFindings.reason: Source-only support for a subcase of codeaudit-19, not a new visual verification.

relatedFindings.title: Hotkey synchronization races the preferences dispatcher
relatedFindings.verification: Recovered HDL log inspected; not triggered in the current fresh session.
relatedFindings.observed: The prior HDL session recorded ConcurrentModificationException in AppPreferences.hotkeySync on java.util.prefs' Event Dispatch Thread.
reproduction: Open Preferences and create/close project windows while preferences change.
Check hotkey updates and app log.
relatedFindings.rootCause: The preferences callback iterates a mutable GUI synchronization list off the Swing event thread.
relatedFindings.fix: Filter preference keys, marshal hotkey changes to the EDT, and manage synchronization listener lifetime safely.
relatedFindings.acceptance: Window creation/destruction concurrent with relevant preference updates produces no exceptions and updates accelerators exactly once.
relatedFindings.reason: Same captured exception as shell-31. User-facing failure in this run was not measured, so no P1 escalation.

harnessFindings.title: Original QA harness isolates preferences but not Java home/autosaves
harnessFindings.observed: Fresh prefs still produced an Autosave found prompt before the app opened. That prompt was not discarded. The corrected launch used a unique fixture basename plus JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-Duser.home=/tmp/logisim-qa-recovery-20260924/remaining-evidence/java-home; jcmd verified both Java home and preference roots.
harnessFindings.fix: Before starting any app, create a per-session home and pass -Duser.home plus the isolated prefs root; isolate config and known app-data paths too. Add startup assertions and unique fixture names. Keep long-lived process ownership explicit. Derive shot dimensions from the actual display or use win for nondefault sizes. Preserve source and jar hash/build provenance.
harnessFindings.acceptance: A fresh session cannot discover or create autosaves in the real user home; two sessions cannot see each other's recovery files. Captures match actual window/display bounds. Cleanup validates and stops only the owning session.
harnessFindings.limits: The original supplied harness itself was not changed. The first launch reached a recovery prompt before isolation was corrected; no original autosave was cleared.
